one_line: Drying of a high-Andean wetland (vega) meadow patch, part of a strip-wide 2023-24 moisture decline that partly recovered in 2025; no mark on the ground.
summary: before.png and after.png (Sentinel-2, 10 m) show a dark-green wetland strip crossing bare Puna desert at 3,770 m with the yellow box on the strip's southern edge; inside the box the two composites are near-identical apart from a slightly browner, smaller dark wet patch at the SW corner, and no new line, pad or spot appears. hires.png (Esri, 2023-03-15, before onset) shows only dense cushion-plant mat with pale dry patches inside the box and no track, pit, structure or object; wayback_strip.png shows the same patch swinging between dense and sparse green across releases from 2014 to 2026. difference.png shows the brightening (red) running along the whole ~1 km strip and the NDVI loss (brown) in the box matched by a larger brown blob ~150 m WNW, so the footprint is one cell of a wetland-wide moisture change. The per-scene series (29 scenes) has no step: inside NBR slides from 0.441 (2023-05-13) to 0.298 (2024-04-07), then recovers to 0.413 (2024-06), 0.424 (2024-12), 0.601 (2025-03) and 0.434 (2025-06), with the ring moving in parallel; the brief itself notes that per-scene values do not separate before from after (shift -0.075 vs noise 0.112, 5 of 11 later scenes show the change), the dossier's own composites give an inside NBR change of only -0.045 (0.379 to 0.335) against the claimed -0.158, and the Landsat 'confirmation' recovers monotonically (NBR 0.168, 0.187, 0.207, 0.248). All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence, converging on the same ordinary cause, and the panel agrees: the change is a reversible drying of living wetland vegetation (SWIR +0.133 dominates, surface_water sub-check drying_signature=true, flat_basin=true, WorldCover 85% grass inside vs 90% bare around), exaggerated into a 'step' by comparing a lush early-May 2023 with a dry early-May 2024 in three-date composites; the landing_trace shape metrics are those of the 8-pixel bounding box (footprint_source bbox, straight_edge_fraction 0.0), not of a real outline.
explanation: Interannual drying of a high-Andean wetland meadow (vega/bofedal cushion-plant mat) at the southern edge of a spring-fed vega strip: the saturated core inside the box shrank and the mat lost water through the 2023 dry season and the weak 2023-24 wet season, then partly recovered in 2025. The same decline covers the whole strip (difference.png) and both sensors record a dip-and-recover, not a persistent mark. The detector's three-date early-May composites turned this gradual, reversible moisture fluctuation into an apparent abrupt step (step_snr 8) that the full per-scene series does not support. Whether the water deficit was rainfall, grazing from the Cavi puesto 1.1 km away, or abstraction at Proyecto Lindero 4.9 km away cannot be told from imagery; none is exotic.
next_step: A Sentinel-2 all-season per-scene NBR/NDWI series through May 2026 for the footprint, the larger NDVI-loss patch ~150 m WNW and the ring: all three following the same dip-and-recover trajectory, with 2026 values back inside the 2018-2023 Apr-May range (NBR 0.43-0.50), closes it as a transient wetland moisture low. A single cloud-free sub-metre image from mid-2024 showing the mat intact with no scar, cut or object would close it outright; CHIRPS/ERA5 precipitation anomalies for the 2023-24 wet season would name the driver.
